blogs.title: Why Orthogonal Finetuning Matters: Preserving Knowledge in Big Models
blogs.description: An easy‑to‑understand overview of orthogonal finetuning (OFT), explaining how multiplying pretrained weights by an orthogonal matrix keeps the geometry of neurons intact, why this matters for preserving pretrained knowledge, and how OFT compares to popular PEFT methods like LoRA and adapters.

blogs.title: From Block‑Diagonal to Butterfly: Making Orthogonal Finetuning Parameter‑Efficient
blogs.description: A dive into the parameter‑efficiency problem of OFT, the limitations of block‑diagonal orthogonal matrices, and the clever solution using butterfly factorizations inspired by the fast Fourier transform. Includes visual analogies and a simple explanation of how sparse matrix products create dense orthogonal transforms with only O(d log d) parameters.

blogs.title: The Information Transmission View: How Graph Theory Helps Design Better Finetuning Layers
blogs.description: Explains the novel perspective of treating orthogonal matrix factorization as an information transmission problem on a grid graph. Shows how thinking about “edges” and “paths” leads to design criteria (dense connectivity, minimal free edges) and why butterfly graphs are optimal for this task.

blogs.title: BOFT vs. LoRA: Spectral Norms, Stability, and Generalization Explained
blogs.description: Compares Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT) with low‑rank approaches such as LoRA. Covers why preserving the spectral norm of pretrained weights leads to more stable training, how BOFT’s structured inductive bias improves generalization, and what the trade‑off between expressivity and regularity looks like in practice.

blogs.title: Putting BOFT to Work: Real‑World Adaptations of Vision Transformers, Language Models, and Diffusion Models
blogs.description: A practical walkthrough of applying BOFT to three different domains—large vision transformers for image classification, large language models for text tasks, and Stable Diffusion for controllable generation. Summarizes key experimental findings and provides tips for practitioners on hyper‑parameters, initialization, and multiplicative dropout.
